1. Load the spotify dataset (available in github repository).
```{r}
spotifyDat <- read_csv("spotifyDat Fall26.csv")
```

2. Create a bar graph of the artist column (Hint: use theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) to rotate the x axis).
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(spotifyDat, aes(artist))+geom_bar()+theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))
```

3. Add genre as a third variable in your graph.
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDat, aes(artist, fill=genre))+geom_bar()+theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))
```

4. Use color brewer to add color to your graph in 3. 
```{r}
library(RColorBrewer)
ggplot(spotifyDat, aes(artist, fill=genre))+geom_bar()+theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))+scale_fill_brewer("Purples")
```

5. Place the legend for the graph you made in 3 on the bottom of the graph. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDat, aes(artist, fill=genre))+geom_bar()+theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))+scale_fill_brewer("Purples")
```

As you probably recognized, the graph you made is really hard to read.

6. Separate the genre column into multiple columns (e.g. so each genre listed is in a unique column)
```{r}
spotifyGenre <- spotifyDat %>% 
  separate(genre, into = c("genre1", "genre2", "genre3", "genre4"), sep = ", ")
```

7. Use these genre columns to create a dataset in long format. 
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
LongspotifyGenre <- pivot_longer(spotifyGenre, cols = c("genre1", "genre2", "genre3", "genre4"), names_to = "genreNumber", values_to = "genre")
```

8.use facet wrap to make graphs of artist by genre 
```{r}
ggplot(LongspotifyGenre, aes(artist))+geom_bar()+theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))+facet_wrap(~genre)
```

9. Create a graph that includes the variables tempo and dancability. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDat, aes(tempo, danceability))+geom_point()
```

10. Add popularity as a third variable. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDat, aes(tempo, danceability, color=popularity))+geom_point()
```

11. Use viridis as a color in your graph from #10
```{r}
library(viridis)
ggplot(spotifyDat, aes(tempo, danceability, color=popularity))+
  geom_point()+
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "mako") #added the c in viridis because the c stands for continuous and popularity is a continuous variable.
```
